After Liquid Glass was first introduced on iOS earlier this year, WhatsApp is now working to extend this design to more interface elements. Here's what you need to know.

Liquid Glass is coming to the WhatsApp drawing editor and video player

Forgive me if this sounds familiar: WhatsApp is expanding the scope of its Liquid Glass redesign, applying the new look to more parts of the app.

After more than six months of testing, WhatsApp rolled out the first wave of Liquid Glass updates more broadly earlier this year.

The company was also looking at applying the new design to elements such as the voice message player, message reactions, and context menus at the time, though those changes remained available only in the test build of the app.

According to WABetaInfo, the latest iOS beta of WhatsApp shows that the company is preparing to extend the Liquid Glass visual style to more interface elements, including the drawing editor and the video player progress bar.

WABetaInfo report:

While it's worth noting that some 9to5Mac readers often report that their iPhones still haven't received the initial Liquid Glass update, the latest news shows that Meta continues to adopt this new visual language across iOS, macOS, and iPadOS.

Back to today's news, WABetaInfo notes that "this feature is still in development and not yet available for testing."
